name: Object-Store Credential Mediator
description: Credential mediator for the object-store modules (typed contracts 1.0: FlatBuffers only; every hostcall an SDS $PIV invocation through sdm_piv). It opens a browser-sealed store credential with the host's keyslot oracle (keyslot.unwrap, gated by wallet_sign) and writes it to the node's machine-bound credential store (secrets.put, the secret on the raw "secret" frame; the username is the access key id) on the lane storage_<store>, under a write grant that is SEPARATE from the read grant. storage/object-s3 holds the read grant alone, so the signer can never overwrite a credential and this module never signs or substitutes anything. ROUTE credential-put: the sealed keyslot envelope is the APR BODY verbatim (the browser's JSON {slotId, ephemeralPublicKey, nonce, ciphertext}) -> keyslot.unwrap -> {username, secret} -> secrets.put; the plaintext is never pushed, logged or returned and is wiped after use. ROUTE credential-clear: secrets.clear, answered identically whether or not a credential was held. ROUTE credential-status: whether the lane is configured (secrets.status) and the node's X25519 wrapping key (node.publicKey) when the host published one. The store name arrives in the APR parameter "store" (1-24 of a-z, 0-9, _) and the lane is derived here as storage_<store>; a refusal is a $QRP KIND Error decision (bad-store 400, unsealed-credential 400, unknown-key-slot 400, unwrap-failed 400, empty-secret 400, username-too-long 400, store-refused 403, clear-refused 403) and no page. No plaintext branch, no echo, no invented key slot.

sequentialJustification.detail: One method over one task: read the task, make at most a handful of synchronous typed hostcalls in a fixed order, emit one decision and one page (or the completed requests). No shared mutable state, no worker pool, no fan-out inside the guest. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles wasi-sequential rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: One task per invocation on the credential port: the $APR ROUTE credential-put | credential-clear | credential-status with PARAMETERS store (and, for put, the sealed envelope as BODY). Success is a $QRP Request decision plus a one-row projection page (store, credentialLane, credentialConfigured, stored|cleared|checked; status adds keySlotId, keySlotPublicKey as raw bytes, keySlotAlgorithm). A surplus frame is refused with error code "batched-input-frames".

acceptedTypeSets.description: SDS $APR task: ROUTE credential-put|credential-clear|credential-status, PARAMETERS store, BODY the sealed envelope verbatim (put).
$QRP decision for foundation/http-respond respond_query: a KIND Request carrying the representation, or a KIND Error with HTTP_STATUS, ERROR_CODE and MESSAGE.

outputPorts.description: The decision for the catalog or credential answer.

acceptedTypeSets.description: $QRP projection page stream: the finished catalog, or the credential lane's new state (providerId, credentialLane, credentialConfigured, stored|cleared). Never a credential value.

outputPorts.description: The answer page (absent on a refusal).

methods.displayName: Serve the credential route over HTTP
methods.description: The HTTP edge of the credential lane: one $HTQ request envelope in (the host is a dumb pipe; routing lives here). GET|PUT|POST|DELETE on a path ending /credentials/<store> becomes the credential-status | credential-put | credential-clear task of mediate and is answered the same way (a $QRP Request decision plus a one-row page, or a $QRP KIND Error: no-route 404, no-store 404, method-not-allowed 405 and the mediate refusals). A credential is never readable back through any route. The flow that mounts it must mark the route NOT anonymous: an anonymous visitor overwriting a node's store credentials would redirect what every viewer's run does.
